# Load Testing Guide

**Owner:** Devon Park · **Status:** Living guide. Written after Sunday Load Test Results - June 27 so the next person doesn't rebuild the harness from scratch.

## When you must load test

- Any new or changed money-movement pipeline, before shadow mode starts.
- Any change to an outbox, queue or batch job that runs at a fixed time.
- Launches expected to add more than 20% to peak traffic on an endpoint.
- Before any cut-over plan includes a date.

When you probably don't: UI changes, low-traffic internal tools, read-only endpoints behind caching.

## The rule we learned in June

Test at **3x** the real peak. 1x proves almost nothing about queues; the interesting failures start at 2x. The ACH pipeline passed 1x comfortably and fell over at 3x because of vacuum contention (Outbox Vacuum Contention Analysis).

## Environment

- `perf` environment: production-sized RDS (db.r6i.4xlarge), real SQS, 3 replicas per Go service, external partners stubbed.
- Stubs simulate realistic latency, including tail latency. The Pillar stub defaults to p50 400ms, p99 6s, with an optional "weekend morning" profile (p99 28s) since Sep 26.
- Run whatever background jobs production runs at that time (the June test only failed because the shadow diff was running too).
- Never point load tests at partner sandboxes without telling the partner.

## Tools

- `replayctl`: replays anonymized production traffic or intents from a chosen day at a multiplier. Source data comes from the anonymized snapshot bucket; Restricted fields are replaced at export.
- `k6` scripts in `perf/scenarios/` for HTTP endpoints.
- Datadog "Perf" dashboard: per-run tags so runs are comparable.

## How to run one

1. Write the pass criteria first. Time-based ("submitted by 12:00 PM PT simulated") beats resource-based ("CPU under 70%").
2. Pick a real reference day. For ACH, the most recent Sunday. For investing, the first beta Monday.
3. Reset `perf` from the latest anonymized snapshot.
4. Run 1x, 2x, 3x in that order. Stop if a run fails; fix before going higher.
5. Capture: throughput, p50/p99 for the hot query or endpoint, queue age, dead tuples on hot tables, CPU and I/O, error counts, duplicates.
6. Write it up using the template below within 2 days.

## What to watch in Postgres

- `n_dead_tup` and last autovacuum on hot tables
- Oldest running transaction (`backend_xmin` age)
- Lock waits
- Index scans vs heap fetches on the claim query

## Report template

- What was tested, against which reference day
- Pass criteria
- Results table per multiplier
- What we saw
- Decision (pass / fail / pass with conditions)
- Follow-ups with owners and dates

## Past runs

| Date | System | Result | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-27 | ACH pipeline | Fail at 3x | Sunday Load Test Results - June 27 |
| 2026-07-25 | ACH pipeline (after fixes) | Pass at 3x and 4x | Outbox Vacuum Contention Analysis |
| 2026-09-02 | `brokerd` funding + orders | Pass at 3x of projected GA week | In this space, investing folder |

The `brokerd` run used projected GA volume: 10% of MTU funding in the first week, with the $2,500/day cap enforced. p99 funding call 210ms at 3x.

## Upcoming

- Round-up sweep on the outbox (ADR-032 - Move Round-up Sweep onto the Outbox Pipeline): 3x of combined ACH plus round-up volume before shadow mode.
- Investing GA week: re-run the `brokerd` scenario with real beta data before go/no-go #2.

Decision: no cut-over date goes into a plan until a 3x test has passed. Marcus Bell and Maya Chen agreed after June.
